author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
habitat: 하천, 호수, 논밭, 바닷가 부근 습지, 물 고인 농경지

months.note: 봄과 가을에 지나가며, 봄철에 특히 많은 수가 보인다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 국내를 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새로, 하천·호수·논밭과 바닷가 근처 습지에 산다. 봄에는 물이 고인 논이나 하천 간척지처럼 얕은 물이 괸 습지에서 전국적으로 많은 수가 눈에 띈다. 곤충과 갑각류를 주로 먹고 조개 같은 연체동물도 잡는다. 축축한 땅에 풀잎과 가는 나뭇가지로 밥그릇 모양 둥지를 틀어 알 4개를 낳고 주로 암컷이 품으며, 세계적으로는 구북구의 툰드라에서 한대와 일부 온대까지 분포한다.

art.subject: Wood Sandpiper (Tringa glareola), adult in breeding plumage as seen in flooded Korean rice fields in late April and May: crown dark brown, finely streaked; a long, bold white supercilium running from the bill to well behind the eye, above a dark loral and eye stripe; upperparts dark brown densely spangled with large whitish and blackish spots and notches; neck and breast whitish, finely streaked grey-brown, the flanks lightly barred; belly and undertail white; white rump; tail white with fine dark bars. Bill dark, slightly paler olive at the base; dark eye; legs yellow to greenish-yellow.
art.pose: wading in shallow water, picking insects from the surface
art.scene: Korean spring wetland: flooded rice paddies with shallow standing water beside a stream; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding plumage (late April–May), side view standing in shallow water: long white supercilium extending behind the eye, dark brown upperparts densely spotted white and black, finely streaked whitish breast, white belly, yellow legs
in flight seen from below: pale greyish-white underwing, white belly, finely barred tail, yellow toes projecting well beyond the tail
in flight seen from above: plain brown wings without a wing-bar, square white rump, white tail with fine dark bars
art.build: Slim, elegant small Tringa, about 22cm, about the length of a Common Starling but slimmer, longer-necked and much longer-legged than Common Sandpiper; stands fairly upright. Bill straight, fine and fairly short, about as long as the head or slightly longer. Legs long, yellowish, with bare tibia; in flight the toes project clearly beyond the tail. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight the wings are brown with no wing-bar, the underwing is pale greyish-white, the white rump is square and the tail finely barred.
avoid: Do not paint a blackish underwing or a blackish back with a supercilium stopping at the eye — those are Green Sandpiper features.
Do not paint grey, black or red legs; the legs are yellowish.
Do not add a white wing-bar or a white wedge in front of the folded wing (Common Sandpiper).
Do not make it large and heavy-billed like a Greenshank, or give it a long needle bill like Marsh Sandpiper.
